subject.title: /acp sessions exposes every gateway ACP session to any allowlisted non-owner sender

question: Should `/acp sessions` remain available to authorized non-owners as a requester-scoped command, or should it become owner/internal-admin-only until requester ownership is modeled?
rationale: The current docs define a non-owner requester-scoped command, but the current implementation is gateway-wide and exposes session metadata, so maintainers should confirm the security boundary before repair.

options.title: Scope Non-Owner Results
options.body: Keep the documented non-owner command but filter results to the current bound/requester session and add two-session regression coverage.

options.title: Make Sessions Owner-Only
options.body: Move `sessions` into the owner/admin gate and update docs/tests if maintainers decide any session listing is too sensitive for non-owners.

options.title: Accept Gateway-Wide Visibility
options.body: Retain the current broad listing only with an explicit maintainer security decision and docs that describe it as owner-equivalent diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Scope Non-Owner Results
recommendation.body: Keep the documented non-owner command but filter results to the current bound/requester session and add two-session regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP metadata/session storage ownership and current-line provenance make this the best available security-boundary routing candidate.
